svg.aria-label: The two-language precompute pipeline and what it ships. The heavy lane runs locally: the same TypeScript engine the browser runs is driven from Node to bake exact pits and Whittle curves, torch trains the two learned models and exports them to ONNX, and Python reshapes everything into traces and manifests. Only the committed artifacts cross into the repository. CI runs the light lane, which needs neither torch nor Node and is a pure function of those artifacts. In the browser the exact optimiser and both ONNX models run live, while the CPIT schedule is rendered from JSON and is never solved live.

The app reads the artifacts at run time, so when
an artifact moves the app moves with it. Prose
does not, which is why prose is what goes stale.
Light lane, the default, and the only lane CI runs
python data-pipeline/run.py all
Reshapes the committed artifacts into the per-case replay traces and manifests. It needs neither torch nor Node, so continuous integration
never retrains and never depends on a GPU, a model download, or a network fetch.
It is a pure function of the committed artifacts: re-running it is byte-identical, because the manifest carries no wall-clock. That is what makes
the replay contract checkable rather than merely claimed.
The two MineLib lanes differ: the benchmark table is baked offline under Node, while the in-app real-case panel fetches an instance and solves it live,
showing its own measured time. Solve times are machine-dependent and vary several-fold between runs; relative errors are not, and do not.
